title: Electricity Generation in Germany, Jan-Oct 2025
author: Federal Statistical Office (synthetic)
text: In the first ten months of 2025, renewable sources supplied 54.2% of German electricity generation, up from 51.6% in the same period of 2024. Wind power contributed 27.1%, photovoltaics 14.8%, biomass 8.3%, and hydropower 4.0%. Net electricity exports fell by 6% year on year. Methodology: plant-level metering data reported under the Energy Statistics Act; provisional figures, revision expected in March 2026.

title: Grid Flexibility Requirements under High Solar Penetration: A German Case Study
author: L. Berger and T. Okafor
text: We model the German grid under photovoltaic shares of 15-25% of annual generation. Our simulations indicate that curtailment rises non-linearly above 18% PV share unless storage capacity grows by at least 2.5 GW per year. Preprint, not yet peer reviewed. Code and data are available in the supplementary repository.

title: Renewables reach record share of German power mix
author: M. Petersen, Daily Chronicle
text: Renewable sources covered about 52% of German electricity consumption in 2023, the grid agency said on Thursday, a record driven by strong wind output in autumn and lower overall demand. Officials cautioned that grid expansion continues to lag behind targets.
